name: Cyberfeminism
summary: Cyberfeminism is a loose feminist current, born in the early 1990s, that treats digital technology and cyberspace as terrain for remaking gender, the body and power. It combines socialist-feminist critique of male-dominated, capitalist technoscience with the hope of appropriating technology for emancipation, and it rejects naturalised identity, the organic family and origin myths.
scope: The 1990s core of VNS Matrix's Cyberfeminist Manifesto, Sadie Plant, the Old Boys Network and Donna Haraway's Cyborg Manifesto (1985) as its main theoretical root, with xenofeminism (Laboria Cuboniks) used as a later offshoot that states the politics more explicitly. It is mostly an art and theory current, not a party programme, so many answers are inferences and the strands differ (VNS rejects reason, XF defends it).

keyFigures.name: Donna Haraway
keyFigures.role: Author of A Cyborg Manifesto (1985), often cited as the genesis of cyberfeminist theory.

keyFigures.name: Sadie Plant
keyFigures.role: British theorist who used the term independently in 1991 and linked women and technology.

sources.title: A Cyborg Manifesto: Science, Technology, and Socialist-Feminism in the Late Twentieth Century
sources.author: Donna Haraway
sources.usedFor: Informatics of domination, affinity not identity, rejection of organic family and goddess origin myths, militarization and welfare erosion.

sources.title: Xenofeminism: A Politics for Alienation
sources.author: Laboria Cuboniks
sources.usedFor: Later cyberfeminist offshoot: gender abolition, anti-naturalism, class abolition, repurposing technology, open-source medicine, reproductive labour.

sources.title: A Cyborg Manifesto
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Secondary summary of Haraway's claims on identity, science, reproduction and nature.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Haraway laments the erosion of the welfare state and women's dependence on it; universal care is inferred from this socialist-feminist concern.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Haraway analyses feminized, precarious homework-economy labour; a higher wage floor is the natural inference but is not argued directly.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Xenofeminism treats markets as no full solution and tech as serving capital's narrow interests; the 1990s strand is similarly anti-capitalist.

public-ownership.rationale: Socialist-feminist framing favours collective control of infrastructure, though no text specifies ownership forms.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Class abolition is named as an aim, so redistributive taxation follows by inference.

unions-good.rationale: Haraway criticises old socialist-feminist unity around the woman worker and calls for coalitions; unions are not specifically endorsed or rejected.

property-fundamental.rationale: Class abolition and open-source models of sharing knowledge cut against strong property rights; inferred.

regulate-corporations.rationale: XF wants technology's gains steered away from capital's narrow interests, implying regulation or more.

cut-welfare.rationale: Haraway treats the dismantling of the welfare state as part of the informatics of domination that hurts women most.

worker-ownership.rationale: Class abolition implies workers controlling production, but cyberfeminist texts rarely propose it concretely.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Haraway warns of surveillance and control as core features of the informatics of domination.

legalize-drugs.rationale: VNS Matrix's pleasure-centred, transgressive stance suggests tolerance, but drug policy is not discussed.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Cyberfeminists contest online harassment but also champion free, disruptive speech; no clear shared line.

strong-leader.rationale: Haraway rejects totalising, single-vision authority and prefers partial, coalitional politics.

state-harmful.rationale: XF calls for new large institutions, not abolition of the state; early strands are rhetorically anti-authority but not anarchist.

limit-guns.rationale: Haraway stresses militarization as a cyborg orgy of domination, so gun control is inferred.

empower-police-military.rationale: Haraway identifies military command-and-control systems as a central apparatus of domination.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: VNS Matrix celebrates sexuality and bodily pleasure and the movement is largely sex-positive; sex work itself is not addressed in the sources.

decide-locally.rationale: Haraway favours affinity coalitions across scales; XF wants mesopolitical institutions; no preference on locality as such.

rehabilitation.rationale: Anti-naturalist, anti-punitive reading of social problems favours rehabilitation, inferred.

traditional-family.rationale: Haraway rejects the organic family as a model of community and XF calls the nuclear family stagnant and isolating.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: XF explicitly includes queer perspectives; marriage as an institution is not discussed, so mild agreement is inferred.

abortion-legal.rationale: XF points to telemedical abortion access as an emancipatory example and cyberfeminism follows Firestone on reproductive autonomy.

more-religion-public.rationale: Haraway says even the goddess is dead and rejects origin myths; public religion contradicts the project.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Black and intersectional cyberfeminism and XF's race abolitionism treat racial inequity as something to correct.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Haraway holds identity is constructed rather than natural, and XF is explicitly gender-abolitionist.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Haraway rejects origin stories and organic unity; national tradition preservation is not a goal, inferred.

gradual-change.rationale: VNS Matrix describes itself as a virus sabotaging dominant discourse, not a gradualist reformer.

reduce-immigration.rationale: XF's generic universalism and anti-exclusion stance imply opposition to restriction; not directly stated.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: XF seeks planetary-scale institutions but cyberfeminists distrust bureaucratic control; no clear stance on the UN.

free-trade.rationale: Anti-capitalist framing and the critique of colonial technology supply chains suggest scepticism of free trade.

nation-first.rationale: Haraway's boundary-blurring, affinity politics and XF's universalism reject nation-first nationalism.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Haraway criticises militarization, so adherents are wary of intervention though human rights concerns pull the other way.

open-borders.rationale: XF's inclusive, anti-exclusion universalism points toward open borders, but it is not stated.

limit-growth.rationale: XF criticises technology's waste in service of markets yet is not degrowth; it wants redirecting growth, not limiting it.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: XF names environmental risk as something to address via technology; climate policy is not the focus.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: XF says technology is not inherently progressive, and Haraway warns against both demonising and trusting it.

expand-nuclear.rationale: No stated view; technophile but sceptical of capital-driven technology, so split.

revolution-justified.rationale: VNS Matrix speaks as saboteurs and virus of the new world disorder, but no explicit endorsement of revolution.

experts-over-public.rationale: Haraway favours situated, partial knowledges and criticises authority claiming a view from nowhere.

central-planning.rationale: XF calls for large-scale institutions but also rejects totalising blueprints; split.

socialized-markets.rationale: XF does not see markets as a full solution but gives no model; inferred neutral.

land-value-tax.rationale: Not addressed and not derivable from principles.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Class abolition implies curbing inherited wealth.

basic-income.rationale: XF wants to free reproductive and family life from wage labour; a basic income is an obvious inference, though not named.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Protectionism is nationalist and at odds with Haraway's boundary-blurring stance.

state-directs-investment.rationale: XF wants technology redirected from market ends, but via which actor is unspecified.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Neither collective nor small-owner property is addressed.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: XF wants family life freed from wage labour demands and class abolished, but not explicitly wage abolition.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: No source I read discusses monetary institutions, and nothing in the core principles settles it, so neutral.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Haraway rejects organic, unified representation in favour of affinity; corporatist bodies are inferred opposed.

one-party-rule.rationale: Haraway opposes totalising unity and single vision in politics.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Hereditary rule rests on organic lineage and origin myths that Haraway rejects, and the movement is anti-patriarchal.

democracy-best.rationale: Coalitional, participatory politics suggests democratic leanings, but the texts are critical of liberal institutions.

direct-votes.rationale: XF models itself on open-source participation but does not discuss referendums.

workers-councils.rationale: Haraway critiques the single worker subject; councils are unaddressed.

right-to-secede.rationale: The texts do not discuss secession; the movement's concerns are gender, body and technology, so neutral.

natural-rulers.rationale: XF rejects appeals to nature as justification for hierarchy.

political-violence-never.rationale: Haraway notes political violence in militarization but does not endorse pacifism; adherents split but lean away from absolute rejection.

war-builds-character.rationale: Haraway portrays war as a cyborg orgy of command and control, not as virtue-building.

separate-church-state.rationale: Haraway rejects goddess and god-based origin stories, so secular politics is inferred.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Haraway says god and goddess are dead; scripture-based law contradicts the project.

private-courts-defense.rationale: XF and Haraway are anti-capitalist; privatised coercion is strongly opposed.

military-superiority.rationale: Haraway criticises militarization and the Star Wars apocalypse as domination.

ethnic-nation.rationale: XF aims to abolish race as a basis of discrimination and rejects essentialist unity.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Haraway critiques Marxist single-subject history; XF treats class abolition as an endpoint but not as history's sole driver.

equal-outcomes.rationale: XF's class and gender abolition aims imply material equality; not framed in these terms.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Critiques noting colonial histories of technology suggest sympathy, but the question is not addressed.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Cyberfeminist critiques attach to colonial legacies; reparations are an inference.

civilizational-union.rationale: Haraway rejects organic unity based on shared origins.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Affinity coalition politics and collective projects run against the celebration of self-interest.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Rejects organic community obligations; emphasis is on bodily autonomy and liberation.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Haraway rejects the nature/culture divide and ecofeminist earth-mother framings.

limit-population.rationale: Reproductive autonomy argues against coercive limits, but no position on policy.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Haraway warns against a demonology of technology and embraces cyborg technoculture.

accelerate-technology.rationale: XF wants to seize and repurpose technology to rebuild society and is willing to disrupt institutions; early cyberfeminism embraced digital spaces.

human-enhancement.rationale: XF endorses open-source DIY hormone and body modification, and Haraway and Plant celebrate the technologised body.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Haraway fears coded control systems, so handing governance to algorithms is viewed with suspicion.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Opposition to surveillance and control implies support, though encryption is not discussed.

restore-past-order.rationale: Haraway says there is no original unity to return to and wants regeneration, not rebirth.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Anti-pragmatist in tone: knowledge is situated and politically committed, not neutral.

direct-action.rationale: VNS Matrix's saboteur and virus language favours disruptive tactics, though XF also works with institutions.

means-match-ends.rationale: XF models itself on open-source participation and mutable platforms; process is part of the aim.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Haraway rejects return to an origin or Eden and embraces technoculture.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: XF wants to liberate reproductive labour but does not target division of labour as such.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Class abolition suggests need-based distribution but it is not stated.

production-for-use.rationale: XF criticises technology serving narrow capital interests, implying production for need.

profit-exploitation.rationale: XF states you are a labourer or poor because you are exploited, and Haraway targets racist male-dominant capitalism.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Haraway rejects the single revolutionary subject and totalising politics.

collective-farming.rationale: Agriculture and land tenure are absent from cyberfeminist writing; neutral by silence.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Haraway links militarism and high-tech capitalism but does not state this thesis.

taxation-theft.rationale: Anti-capitalist, collectivist stance rejects the claim.

harm-principle.rationale: VNS Matrix rejects moral codes in favour of pleasure; a liberal harm test is not their frame.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Coalitional, affinity-based politics treats groups as political actors.

conscription.rationale: Opposition to militarization implies rejecting conscription.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Participatory, coalitional politics emphasises voice over exit.

state-as-business.rationale: Anti-capitalist; treating citizens as customers contradicts the project.

positive-liberty.rationale: XF's access-to-tools, healthcare and freedom from wage labour implies freedom requires material means.

media-academia-power.rationale: Not a concern of the movement, which instead stresses corporate and military technoscience power.

hereditarian-race.rationale: XF treats racialised traits as no basis for discrimination and rejects naturalising claims.

organic-representation.rationale: Haraway rejects the organic family as a model for community.

total-state.rationale: Rejects totalising politics; XF seeks mutable platforms.

national-rebirth.rationale: Haraway prefers regeneration to rebirth and rejects origin myths.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Haraway's critique of militarism and rejection of origin-based identity makes imperial expansion alien to the movement.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Hierarchical personal loyalty conflicts with affinity coalitions.

bound-labor.rationale: Tying workers to land under a lord contradicts XF's aim of abolishing class and exploitation.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Haraway argues for situated, partial knowledges and no innocent standpoint.

universal-morality.rationale: Haraway rejects totalising theory, though XF defends a generic universal built from particular struggles.

single-common-good.rationale: Haraway prefers partial perspectives and affinity coalitions over a single reasoned good.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Cyberfeminism has no stated position on Zionism or any national homeland; neutral.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: No source addresses diaspora return rights; neutral by silence.

revive-national-language.rationale: Not addressed; mildly cut by anti-origin-myth stance.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Class abolition suggests democratic control of work.

school-vouchers.rationale: Marketisation of public goods is not favoured.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Austerity impacts on women are an anti-welfare cut, so inferred opposed.

economic-freedom.rationale: XF treats markets as no full solution and criticises technology serving capital, so it does not hold that political freedom rests on market freedom.

rule-by-example.rationale: Haraway rejects authority grounded in organic or moral origins; rulers' virtue as a basis for rule is foreign to this politics.

force-without-un.rationale: Haraway's critique of militarization makes unilateral force abroad objectionable, though this is inferred.

reason-over-faith.rationale: XF defends reason as a tool for emancipation, while VNS Matrix explicitly rejects reason in favour of pleasure and madness; strands split.

work-for-welfare.rationale: XF seeks freedom from wage labour; conditional welfare conflicts.

class-collaboration.rationale: Class abolition implies conflict, not partnership.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: VNS Matrix is iconoclastic but there is no statement on cultural institutions.

dominated-front.rationale: Anti-Western-bloc fronts are not discussed in the sources; neutral.

workers-nation.rationale: Haraway rejects organic and national unity and affinity coalitions cross borders, so a nationally bounded working class is opposed.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: XF is gender-abolitionist; Haraway rejects naturalised identity.

ban-interest.rationale: Usury is not discussed by cyberfeminists; neutral by silence.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: XF explicitly aims to make racialised traits no basis for discrimination, so legal segregation is strongly rejected.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Haraway offers a nuanced analysis of power rather than the instrumental thesis.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Environmental risk is seen as a concern; not central.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Hybridity and rejection of natural identity favour plural belonging.

elite-replacement.rationale: Conspiratorial nativist claim is opposed to universalist, inclusive politics.

proportional-representation.rationale: Electoral systems are not discussed in the sources; neutral.

national-mission.rationale: Missionary nationalism clashes with Haraway's anti-origin politics and her critique of militarized domination.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: VNS Matrix targets male-dominated technology and culture and Haraway names racist male-dominant capitalism.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: VNS Matrix is anti-establishment, but corruption is not the framing.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Opposes eugenic coercion and bodily control over reproduction.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Rejects racial essentialism; hybridity is celebrated.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: XF's universalism and abolition of gender and race hierarchy express equal worth.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Debates among Marxist-Leninists about one-country socialism are outside the cyberfeminist canon; neutral.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Critiques of colonial technology exist but no stated view.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Personal-law questions are not addressed by the movement's texts; neutral.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Individual freedom of identity and anti-religious-authority stance opposes it.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Not a cyberfeminist concern; no source addresses it, so neutral.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Totalising state strengthening conflicts with anti-authoritarian leanings.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilism is a national-interest frame at odds with the movement.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: VNS Matrix celebrates sabotage; libertarian non-aggression is not in the frame.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Haraway rejects antagonistic dualisms and favours coalition.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: No source addresses militant democracy; adherents' views are unknown, so neutral.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Resistance to domination is central, but the republican formulation is not used.

separated-powers.rationale: Constitutional design is not discussed in the sources; neutral.

vanguard-party.rationale: Haraway rejects the single revolutionary subject and unity imposed from above.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Class abolition suggests priority to the exploited.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Housing tenure policy is not addressed by the movement; neutral.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: XF says people are poor because they are exploited.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Haraway advocates affinity across difference and hybridity.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Sortition is not discussed, though XF's participatory ethos could cut either way; neutral.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Concern with surveillance and control rejects it.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Price controls are not addressed in any source; neutral.

party-controls-media.rationale: Control of communications is a form of the informatics of domination.

party-commands-army.rationale: Militarism and party-state concentration both opposed.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: XF's inclusive universalism points against long waits for citizenship, though this is inferred rather than stated.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Pay caps for representatives are not discussed; neutral.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Haraway favours affinity coalitions over imposed unity, so binding party discipline is inferred disfavoured.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: The EU model is not discussed in the sources; neutral.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Concentrating military command in an executive runs against Haraway's critique of command-and-control militarism.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Church governance is not discussed, but the movement's anti-hierarchy and secular stance disfavour episcopal rule.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: VNS Matrix rejects moral codes and uses provocative art.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Open-ended personal tenure conflicts with the movement's suspicion of concentrated, single-vision authority.

recall-officials.rationale: Recall mechanisms are not discussed in the sources; neutral.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Anti-militarist, but nationalist withdrawal is not their frame.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Not addressed; mild opposition to homeowner-family model.

people-in-arms.rationale: Haraway treats militarization as a core domination apparatus, so an armed citizenry is inferred opposed, though the idea is not discussed.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Haraway rejects organic and nature-based nostalgia; the cyborg is urban and technological.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: National reunification is not addressed by the movement; neutral.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Situated knowledges are valued; anti-intellectualism opposed.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: XF rejects Eurocentric universalism and seeks plural coalitions.

death-penalty.rationale: Anti-militarist and anti-punitive leanings imply rejection.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Bodily knowledge and gender equality are core, as with XF's open-source medicine.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: XF defends science and reason as emancipatory.

restrict-pornography.rationale: VNS Matrix's sex-positive, transgressive stance opposes bans, though feminist anti-porn views exist.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Haraway rejects belonging grounded in origin and organic kinship, so descent-based citizenship is opposed.

minority-language-support.rationale: Pluralist, inclusion-minded politics implies support for minority languages, though the sources do not mention them.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Exemptions for religious practice are not discussed; the movement is anti-religious authority but pro-pluralism, so neutral.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: VNS Matrix celebrates madness, disorder and hybrid identity; Haraway embraces fluid identities.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Critiques of colonial technology imply sympathy.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: National independence movements are not a topic of the texts; neutral.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Constitutional rewriting procedures are not discussed; neutral.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Developmental authoritarianism conflicts with the movement's anti-authoritarian, anti-control stance.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Critique of access privilege implies duty to share technology and resources.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Haraway names the Star Wars apocalypse as emblem of domination, so national nuclear weapons are opposed by inference.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The mode of choosing a head of state is not addressed; neutral.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Central bank design is not addressed; neutral.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Territorial claims based on origin are rejected.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Class abolition implies property subordinate to social ends.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: The Soviet Union's character is not addressed in the cyberfeminist texts; neutral.

precautionary-principle.rationale: XF says technology needs interfaces accounting for its risks, but no stance on the principle.

collective-defense.rationale: Alliance doctrine is not addressed; the movement's anti-militarism is offset by lack of a stated view, so neutral.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: International law on annexation is not discussed; neutral.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: The movement is anti-religious-authority but also wary of state control, so adherents are split.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Ceremonial heads of state are not discussed; neutral.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Haraway's critique of militarized coercion suggests opposition to using force to hold a country together, inferred.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Special-autonomy arrangements are not addressed; neutral.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Contradicts the rejection of gods, goddesses and origins.

character-from-environment.rationale: Identity as constructed and affinity-based rather than natural.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Unaccountable rule contradicts the movement's resistance to domination, inferred from Haraway's politics.

space-expansion.rationale: Techno-optimism present but not stated about space.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Classical constitutional theory is not engaged by the texts; neutral.

leader-cult.rationale: Haraway's rejection of single vision and totalising unity makes cults of a national leader alien to the movement.

equal-parenting.rationale: Gender-abolitionist, but court presumptions are not addressed.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Debates on class struggle after a revolution are outside the cyberfeminist texts; neutral.

land-redistribution.rationale: Agrarian reform is not addressed in the sources; neutral.

refugee-return.rationale: Right-of-return questions are not addressed; neutral.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Haraway rejects origin and descent as grounds for political belonging, so irredentism based on nationality is opposed.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Individual freedom of identity and rejection of religious authority.

women-must-cover.rationale: VNS Matrix celebrates the female body and sexuality; coercion contradicts XF and Haraway.

common-currency.rationale: Monetary union is not addressed; neutral.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Haraway rejects unity founded on shared ancestry and organic kinship, so such unions are opposed.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Minority autonomy schemes are not addressed in the sources; neutral.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Emigration versus homeland-building is not addressed; neutral.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Haraway critiques Marxist history yet treats economic restructuring as shaping politics.

ban-cartels.rationale: Competition law is not discussed in the sources, so neutral.

no-bailouts.rationale: Bailout policy is not addressed; neutral by silence.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Rights of marginalised groups should limit majorities.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: XF seeks to break male dominance in science and institutions.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Autarkic blocs rest on national or imperial boundaries that Haraway's boundary-blurring politics rejects.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Pro-labour and anti-exploitation, so binding standards fit.

moral-incentives.rationale: Incentive design is not addressed by the sources; neutral.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Opposes militarization; foco strategies are totalising.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Anti-hierarchy politics and XF's class abolition imply opposition to inherited rank, though not specifically stated.

history-own-civilization.rationale: XF rejects Eurocentric universalism and favours plural, intersectional perspectives, so a civilization-centred curriculum is disfavoured.

patriotic-education.rationale: Teaching national pride is at odds with Haraway's anti-origin stance and XF's universalism.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Cyberfeminist and XF commitments to racial justice imply defending race-conscious remedies, inferred.

public-money-creation.rationale: Money creation is not addressed; neutral.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Haraway describes capitalism restructuring into the informatics of domination, so it adapts, but with no verdict.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Cyberfeminist critique of the colonial histories behind technology implies opposition to neo-imperial influence.

delink-world-market.rationale: Dependency-theory delinking is not discussed in the sources; neutral.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Theories of the labour aristocracy are not engaged by the sources; neutral.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: XF treats gender and race hierarchies as injustices to abolish, so a right to discriminate is rejected.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Constitutional entrenchment is not discussed; neutral.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Legal status of colonial treaties is not addressed; neutral.

elective-rulers.rationale: Hereditary succession depends on organic lineage that the movement rejects, so elective rule is mildly favoured by inference.

minority-veto.rationale: Consensus veto rules are not discussed; neutral.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Resistance to domination is a core theme, so resisting a ruler who breaks the law is an inferred yes.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Parliamentary supremacy is not discussed; neutral.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Haraway discusses blurred human-animal boundaries and does not treat animals as lesser, but not a stated welfare position.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Animal-use ethics are not discussed in the sources; neutral.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Replaces paternalistic charity with structural redistribution and class abolition.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Haraway and VNS Matrix are explicitly political.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Haraway describes media and communication systems as part of control, but the movement also uses media subversively.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Haraway treats power as networked communication-based control; hegemony is not named.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Critiques of colonial roots of technology support this, inferred.

native-born-offices.rationale: Reserving offices for native-born citizens conflicts with XF's inclusive universalism and Haraway's rejection of origin.

party-own-road.rationale: Inter-party relations among communist parties are not discussed; neutral.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Development strategy is not addressed; neutral.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Territorial claims based on past ownership rest on origin myths Haraway rejects, so revanchism is opposed.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Not addressed in the sources, and indigenous claims may conflict with their rejection of origin-based authority; neutral.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Their anti-hierarchy, anti-authoritarian politics implies sympathy for anti-fascism as a constitutional value, though this is inferred.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: The comparative-totalitarianism debate is not addressed; neutral.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: XF's critique of colonial and racial legacies suggests sympathy for removing or recontextualising such monuments, inferred.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Gender-abolitionist but structural patriarchy is stressed; split.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Patriarchy framing implies asymmetry in violence.

paid-care-work.rationale: XF treats reproductive labour as an economic and political issue to be liberated and recognised.

filial-duty.rationale: Haraway rejects the organic family as a model for community, so lifelong filial obligation is not part of the politics.

office-by-exam.rationale: Imperial-style examination systems are not discussed; neutral.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Economic nationalism is at odds with boundary-blurring.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Rejects the organic family and supports individual freedom within households.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Imperative mandates are not discussed in the sources; neutral.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Privatised, individualised welfare conflicts with the socialist-feminist concern for collective provision, inferred.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Land tenure systems are not addressed; neutral.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Parliamentary budget control is not addressed; neutral.

single-official-language.rationale: Pluralist, anti-universalist politics disfavours enforced monolingualism, though language policy is not discussed.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Nationalist land restrictions are in tension with boundary-blurring politics, mildly opposed by inference.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Structural view of oppression suggests agreement.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: XF criticises technology in service of waste and markets.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Haraway's critique of militarization and covert command systems implies opposition to arming proxies, inferred.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Imperial domination of allied states contradicts the movement's anti-domination politics, inferred.

corporate-influence.rationale: Haraway targets male-dominant capitalism and techno-corporate power.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Not addressed; mild opposition to sovereignty-based control.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Cyberfeminism since Firestone defends reproductive autonomy and Haraway uncouples cyborgs from organic reproduction, so state natalism is disfavoured.

residents-only-property.rationale: Exclusionary local property rules cut against inclusive universalism but housing is not discussed; mildly opposed.

job-guarantee.rationale: XF wants freedom from precarious wage labour and Haraway describes the insecurity of homework-economy work, so a job guarantee is inferred favoured.

democratic-peace.rationale: International-relations theory is not addressed in the sources; neutral.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Anarchic spirit of sabotage but no explicit stance.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: XF criticises Eurocentric universalism that passes particular identities off as neutral, and the movement notes colonial histories of technology.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: XF rejects Eurocentric universalism but also defends a generic universal; no clear stance on diverging political forms.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Haraway sees military command-and-control as a core apparatus of domination, so an armed-forces guardian role is rejected.

non-intervention.rationale: Not addressed by cyberfeminist texts; the strands reject military intervention but also state boundaries.

industrial-unions.rationale: Not addressed directly; Haraway discusses restructured, feminised labour but takes no side on union form.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Inferred from the universalist, anti-essentialist politics that rejects naturalised identity and origin myths; conspiracy claims against a minority are the opposite.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Xenofeminism calls for overhauling the nuclear family unit and Haraway rejects the organic family; ending state-conferred marriage is inferred from that, not stated.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Inferred from the open-source and repurposed-technology outlook and the critique of technology serving capital.

local-production.rationale: Xenofeminism says politics that exclusively valorise the local are insufficient and favours scaling up beyond the microcommunity.

informal-organisation.rationale: Xenofeminism stands against sheer horizontalism and autonomous zones in favour of large-scale collective organisation.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Inferred from the universalist, anti-nationalist stance (nation-first is rejected); not stated as a legal doctrine.

religious-nation.rationale: Xenofeminism calls essentialist naturalism theology-like and rejects any natural basis for political justification; defining a nation by religion is inferred as opposed.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Inferred from its rejection of hierarchy and domination; Haraway's critique of the informatics of domination extends to imperial order.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Inferred from its socialist-feminist solidarity and rejection of localism and fixed boundaries.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Haraway's socialist feminism criticises property relations but it never addresses personal belongings versus productive property.

defeat-communism.rationale: Inferred from its socialist-feminist roots that adherents would not campaign to defeat communism.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: The current is not concerned with who delivers public services; adherents are split between statist and anti-statist views.

religion-illusion.rationale: Haraway prefers the cyborg to the goddess and the movement rejects origin myths and the naturalised; secular materialism is inferred, not stated as a theory of religion.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Haraway and Xenofeminism criticise capitalist technoscience as a system of domination, while still wanting its technologies appropriated.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Haraway's socialist-feminism ties women's position to the restructured homework economy and capitalist technoscience, so change in economic organisation is needed.

socialized-care.rationale: Xenofeminism and Haraway call for reorganising reproduction and the family away from private households; public provision is inferred from this.

purge-loanwords.rationale: The current celebrates hybridity, mutation and impurity, so a purge of foreign words would run against its central metaphors; this is inferred.

treaties-binding.rationale: Treaties with internal nations are not addressed and adherents have no common view.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Xenofeminism explicitly rejects localism and folk politics; small communal communities are inferred as not favoured.

majority-settlement.rationale: Inferred from its rejection of naturalised identity and ethnic belonging and its internationalism.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Haraway calls herself a socialist feminist and XF is anti-capitalist, but the current does not frame a third way between capitalism and communism.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from its rejection of origin myths and naturalised identity.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from its socialist-feminist, anti-reactionary politics.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Its rejection of naturalised gender and the organic body, and its support for queer and trans bodies, rule out criminalising same-sex relations.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from its emancipatory, anti-authoritarian politics.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from its anti-origin-myth, anti-patriarchal stance toward religion.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from its socialist-feminist, anti-imperial critique of power.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from its secular stance and its distance from religious politics.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from its secular stance and distrust of violent politics.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from its aim of appropriating technology so ordinary people can reshape the structures governing them.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Haraway's socialist-feminism and xenofeminism explicitly link gender, race and class domination and reject single-issue politics.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: It treats gender as constructed and open to remaking, and xenofeminism explicitly supports trans and gender-fluid bodies.

assisted-dying.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from its stress on bodily autonomy and technological intervention in the body.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Not addressed; it borrows from several traditions and does not frame itself on that axis, though it is left in practice. Inferred.

alienated-labor.rationale: Its socialist-feminist critique of capitalist technoscience treats labour under capital as dominating workers, which is the alienation the statement describes.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from its anti-essentialist, anti-xenophobic politics.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from its secular, anti-patriarchal and anti-origin-myth stance.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Not addressed; religion is not a theme and adherents' views on state dress rules are not documented.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from its feminist aim of ending power imbalances that silence women.

social-market-economy.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from its anti-capitalist critique, which also distrusts a state-run economy, so a mixed model is only mildly rejected.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from its anti-militarist, anti-patriarchal feminist roots.

rich-first.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from its egalitarian, anti-capitalist politics.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Not addressed; no documented position on military blocs.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Inferred from its rejection of origin myths and the organic family, which hereditary rule relies on.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Not addressed by the cyberfeminist sources.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Inferred from Haraway's socialist-feminist concern with institutions that remove women's economic support.

property-franchise.rationale: Inferred from its socialist-feminist politics, which oppose wealth-based exclusion from political life.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Haraway criticises ecofeminism's organic, naturalised links between women and nature, and xenofeminism rejects nature as a guide, though both analyse shared structures of domination.

reification.rationale: Inferred from the socialist-feminist critique of capitalist technoscience and the informatics of domination.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Inferred from the socialist-feminist view that formal rights are hollow where capital controls communication and media.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Not addressed; strands differ, with VNS Matrix rejecting reason and legal order and xenofeminism defending universalism.

racial-franchise.rationale: Haraway's manifesto criticises racism and the politics of racial identity, and xenofeminism rejects naturalised exclusion.

online-participation.rationale: Cyberfeminism treats the internet and cyberspace as a main arena for feminist politics and collective action.

open-government-data.rationale: Inferred from its open-technology and anti-gatekeeping commitments.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Inferred from its rejection of naturalised identities and restrictions on bodies and relationships.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Inferred from its opposition to naturalised identity and exclusion.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Inferred from Xenofeminism's horizontal, participatory politics and Haraway's affinity-based coalitions; assemblies by lot are not discussed.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Haraway rejects origin myths and the organic family and VNS Matrix rejects inherited moral codes, so adherents would update doctrine at least; inferred, since they mostly reject religion.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Haraway's socialist-feminism criticises capitalist technoscience and the feminised, precarious economy; concern for wealth power is inferred from this.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Inferred from cyberfeminism's rejection of fixed gender and sexual identity, though Haraway also condemns militarisation.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Haraway rejects origin myths and goddess religion, but the sources give no view on the state teaching unbelief; inferred.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Not addressed; Haraway criticises militarised policing technology but the sources give no abolition programme.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Not addressed; cyberfeminism rejects naturalised identity categories but offers no view on constitutional power-sharing.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Haraway laments the erosion of welfare and women's dependence on it, implying reliance on state provision rather than charity; inferred.

term-limits.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; adherents would have no common view.

vote-delegation.rationale: Open-source and networked collective ideas suggest sympathy, but the sources do not discuss voting systems.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Xenofeminism favours technological futures but the sources do not discuss extinction risk.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Inferred from opposition to gender hierarchy and the naturalised organic family.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Haraway rejects the organic family and xenofeminism aims to end gender as a grid of unequal power, so spouses should be equals.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Haraway's politics of affinity rather than identity points toward inclusive membership, though local voting is not discussed.

rent-control.rationale: Haraway analyses women's precarious dependence on housing and welfare in the homework economy; rent caps are an inference from this.

abolish-ip.rationale: Xenofeminism calls for open-source repurposing of technology and medicine, so weakening patents is inferred, but abolition is not stated.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Haraway's critique of militarisation and of command-and-control informatics implies rejection of drilled national-service youth movements.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Haraway criticises militarised technoscience and Star Wars-era weapons; the stance on basing is inferred from it.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Inferred from Haraway's critique of militarisation and of the informatics of domination.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; the current is mostly art and theory.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Xenofeminism aims at class abolition and attends to reproductive labour, implying income should track work, not property.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: The cyborg is unfaithful to origin and Haraway is not a pacifist; the topic is not addressed.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Haraway rejects origin myths and naturalised identities, and the cyborg has no origin story to claim.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Xenofeminism is anti-naturalist and Haraway treats nature and bodies as constructed by science and culture.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Haraway argues for affinity instead of identity and says there is nothing that naturally makes the category 'women'.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Inferred from the rejection of origin myths and naturalised communities; martyrdom cults are not discussed.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: VNS Matrix is bodily, ironic and rejects moral codes; a good-versus-evil spiritual framing is inferred to be unwelcome.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Diasporas and homelands are not discussed.

culture-before-state.rationale: Nation-building is not an object of cyberfeminism; no position is documented.

god-not-male.rationale: Haraway rejects the male-sky-god and goddess myths of origin; gendering God exclusively as male is inferred to be rejected.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Haraway rejects both patriarchal religion and goddess spirituality and does not set out a test for scripture.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Haraway's affinity politics rejects privileging any natural identity group, so reserving economic life for a majority is inferred to be opposed.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Haraway's affinity politics rejects bounded natural units of people; this is an inference.

independent-unions.rationale: Unions are not discussed; Haraway analyses women's precarious labour but gives no line on union independence.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Haraway's socialist-feminism ties emancipation to the power of the people who do the work; inferred, not argued as a definition of socialism.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Haraway laments erosion of public welfare provision; keeping local essentials public is inferred from that concern.

second-chamber.rationale: Constitutional design is not addressed; adherents have no stated view on bicameralism.

municipal-property.rationale: Property forms are not addressed beyond critiquing capitalist technoscience; no stated view on municipal ownership.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Haraway's affinity politics favours non-hierarchical coalitions, but confederal structures are not discussed, so this is left neutral.

family-wage.rationale: Haraway critiques the family wage and the male-breadwinner household as part of the 'homework economy' analysis; inferred rejection of a wage built around a family.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Xenofeminism calls for open-source, accessible medicine and repurposing technology; faster approval is inferred, not stated.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Xenofeminism embraces technoscientific remaking of the body and rejects naturalised limits; support for ageing research is inferred.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Cyberfeminism values pseudonymous and bodily-free action beyond state control; payment privacy is inferred from its anti-surveillance stance.

online-anonymity.rationale: Online anonymity and shifting identities are central to cyberspace as a site for remaking gender; strand-wide but not stated as a policy.

person-over-state.rationale: Haraway rejects unitary humanist subjects and organic wholes, but also opposes domination by collectives; adherents are split.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Haraway prefers cyborg to goddess and rejects origin myths of spiritual wholeness; spiritual politics is inferred to be unwelcome.

gm-crops.rationale: Xenofeminism calls for repurposing technology for emancipation and rejects naturalism; GM crops are inferred as acceptable.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Haraway's affinity-not-identity politics rejects organising on naturalised identity categories, and cyberfeminism criticises race-blind whiteness; inferred.

racial-pride.rationale: Not addressed; cyberfeminism criticises racial essentialism but also supports marginalised groups' self-assertion.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Haraway analyses militarization of technology as part of the informatics of domination; inferred preference for defensive-only force.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Inferred: Haraway and xenofeminism reject naturalised identity and origin myths, which includes organic nations.

communal-electorates.rationale: Inferred from its rejection of fixed identity categories; separate religious electorates are not discussed.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Inferred: the current is internationalist and sees no national in-group to protect; it is not discussed.

free-public-college.rationale: Inferred from Haraway's socialist-feminist concern for the welfare state and xenofeminism's demand for universal access to technoscience.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Not addressed by the core texts; adherents are split between eco-feminist and accelerationist leanings.

future-generations.rationale: Haraway rejects origin myths and organic redemption narratives, while xenofeminism is future-oriented; the texts state no duty to the next generations.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Haraway and xenofeminism reject essentialist claims about women's nature and any gendered distinct-values stance, with some strands disagreeing.

arms-reduction.rationale: Haraway notes the military origins of cyborg technology but the texts take no position on armament levels.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Not addressed in the core texts.

capital-controls.rationale: Socialist-feminist critique of capitalist technoscience implies hostility to global capital, but no specific position on controls is stated.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Inferred from the manifestos' distrust of state and military power; no stated position on who may bear arms.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Haraway describes the cyborg as an illegitimate offspring of militarism and the current rejects militarised masculinity, so refusal is inferred.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Inferred from the socialist-feminist critique of capitalist labour, which favours worker organisation over individual contracts.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Not addressed; a welfare top-up may be seen as useful or as a half-measure within capitalism.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Inferred from the anti-capitalist, state-using politics of xenofeminism, which would resist constraints on public spending.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Haraway's 'informatics of domination' analysis covers the global homework economy that exploits women in poorer countries, from which reform of its rules is inferred.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Xenofeminism wants to build scaled-up institutions rather than only tear down, while Haraway is hostile to the state; adherents are split.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Xenofeminism calls for experimentation and rejects fixed blueprints, so open experimentation is inferred.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Inferred from the rejection of treating nature as a resource for domination and from the anti-commodification stance.

sacred-nation.rationale: The current rejects organic wholes, origin myths and naturalised identity, which includes sacralised nations.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Inferred from socialist-feminist egalitarianism; the sources never discuss student debt.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Haraway's emphasis on women of colour and unequal global structures makes a core-periphery exploitation analysis congenial, though not stated for regions.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Xenofeminism argues that nothing about the human should be treated as given and Haraway rejects an original unity or fixed nature.

public-service-media.rationale: Inferred from support for public provision and wariness of commercial and state control of communication; not stated.

missingStatements.text: Gender should be abolished as a basis for unequal power.
missingStatements.rationale: Xenofeminism states that it is gender-abolitionist, aiming to end gender as a grid for unequal power, and Wikipedia describes cyberfeminism as seeking to dissolve identity boundaries.
missingStatements.declined: Covered by patriarchy-structural, gender-social-construct and equal-moral-worth.

missingStatements.text: Women and marginalised groups should seize and repurpose existing technologies rather than reject them.
missingStatements.rationale: Haraway warns against a demonology of technology and XF urges using the master's tools; VNS Matrix describes infiltrating electronic spaces.
missingStatements.declined: Covered by tech-solves-problems, accelerate-technology and human-enhancement.

notes: Strands differ: VNS Matrix rejects reason and moral codes while xenofeminism defends reason; early cyberfeminism was criticised for white, cisgender and affluent perspectives. Cyberfeminism is an art and theory current, so economic and constitutional statements are mostly inferred low-confidence answers.
